source_meta._title: Goats loaded from older worlds lose their horns

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, single-player. Create and save a disposable source world in Java Edition 1.18.2 as the deterministic pre-22w17a version, then open that exact same world in affected snapshot 22w17a. Use Creative mode only to obtain and place a goat deterministically; Creative mode is an execution convenience rather than a reported requirement.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher must be able to launch the exact Java Edition versions 1.18.2 and 22w17a. If snapshots are hidden, enable the launcher option that makes historical snapshots available when creating an installation.

Both installations must use the same game directory so that the 22w17a installation can access the world created in 1.18.2. If separate game directories are necessary, copy the complete source-world folder into the 22w17a game directory before opening it.
Use a new, disposable test world. Opening it in 22w17a may upgrade its saved data.
Do not create the source world directly in 22w17a, and do not open it in fix version 1.19 Pre-release 2 before this test.

The plan assumes default controls: E opens the inventory, number keys select hotbar slots, right-click uses the selected item, and Esc opens the pause menu. Use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
No world seed, coordinates, dedicated server, additional player, resource pack, or datapack is specified by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation using the exact Java Edition version 1.18.2, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, give the disposable test world a recognizable name, and set Game Mode to Creative. Leave the seed and other settings at their defaults, then create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new 1.18.2 single-player world begins loading in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait without leaving the world until the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, the loading overlay is gone, and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Move to a flat, unobstructed patch of ground close to the player's current position so that a goat placed there will be easy to see after reloading the world.
steps.success_cue: There is a visible solid ground block within right-clicking distance and enough open space for a goat.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, enter the item name, and move one Goat Spawn Egg into any hotbar slot at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Goat Spawn Egg is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the hotbar slot containing the Goat Spawn Egg using its number key or the mouse wheel, aim at the nearby ground, and right-click once to place one goat.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one goat is standing near the player, and the Goat Spawn Egg is the selected hotbar item.

steps.action: Keep the goat and its surrounding chunk loaded by remaining close to it. Face the goat and confirm before conversion that this source goat is fully rendered and has its normal visible horns. Do not make it ram a block or otherwise interact with its horns.
steps.success_cue: The goat is visible close to the player in the 1.18.2 world, its horns are visible, and the player remains near it.

steps.action: While still close to and facing the goat, press Esc and select Save and Quit to Title. Do not first travel away from the goat.
steps.success_cue: The single-player world closes and the 1.18.2 main menu appears, indicating that the nearby goat and player position have been saved.

steps.action: Exit the 1.18.2 game client completely so that the launcher can start a different version without keeping the world open.
steps.success_cue: The 1.18.2 game window is closed and the Minecraft Launcher is available.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation using the exact affected snapshot 22w17a, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as snapshot 22w17a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and select the exact world created and saved in 1.18.2. Verify it is the same world by its name; do not create a new world.
steps.success_cue: The 1.18.2 source world is highlighted in the 22w17a world-selection screen.

steps.action: Open the selected source world in 22w17a. If an older-world or experimental-version safety prompt appears, choose the option that backs up and then loads the world, or the equivalent option that confirms opening it. Allow any backup operation to finish and do not cancel world loading.
steps.success_cue: The world-loading screen starts and 22w17a begins loading or converting the world that was saved in 1.18.2.

steps.action: Wait until the upgraded world has completely loaded, nearby terrain is rendered, and player movement responds normally. Without leaving the area, locate the same goat that was saved close to the player. Do not spawn a replacement goat in 22w17a; if the saved goat is absent, reset and repeat from the 1.18.2 source-world setup.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the same world under 22w17a, the saved area and goat entity are loaded, and the player is positioned close enough for the separate observation agent to inspect the goat.

stor.handoff_condition: The pre-22w17a world has just been opened and converted by 22w17a, loading the goat that was created and saved in 1.18.2. The surrounding terrain is rendered, movement is responsive, and the saved goat is visible at close range. Hand control to the observation subsystem before evaluating the goat's appearance.
uncertainties: The report requires a world from before 22w17a but does not identify one exact source version. Java Edition 1.18.2 is selected as a deterministic pre-22w17a release containing goats.

The report does not specify a game mode or how the source goat was obtained. Creative mode and a Goat Spawn Egg are used to avoid dependence on biome generation, natural spawning, exploration, or commands.

The phrase 'make sure goats are loaded in' is ambiguous. This plan operationalizes it by placing a goat near the player, waiting for it to render, remaining in its chunk, and saving the world while still beside it.
The report does not specify whether an upgrade or backup prompt appears when opening the 1.18.2 world in 22w17a, so the prompt-handling instruction is conditional.

No deterministic seed, coordinates, or method of containing the goat is supplied. The player therefore saves immediately beside the goat and must reset rather than substituting a newly created 22w17a goat if the saved goat cannot be located.

source_meta._title: Items fields with old boolean JSON formatting are cleared upon world update

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft: Java Edition in single-player. Create and save the test world in release 1.20.2, then open that exact same save in release 1.20.4. Use Survival mode with commands enabled so the ordinary player-inventory interface is available. Both installations must use the same game directory, or the saved world must be copied unchanged from the 1.20.2 saves directory to the 1.20.4 saves directory.
preconditions: The launcher or test harness can start the exact Java Edition releases 1.20.2 and 1.20.4. If necessary, create separate launcher installations by selecting those releases in the installation version selector. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Launcher?utm_source=openai))
Use a new, disposable test world rather than an important existing world.
Run a vanilla client without mods, datapacks, or third-party world-conversion tools.
Ensure the 1.20.2 and 1.20.4 launches can access the same world save; do not recreate the world in 1.20.4.
Do not open the test world in any intermediate, snapshot, or later version between the 1.20.2 save and the 1.20.4 load.

Use default controls where available: T opens chat, E opens inventory, Esc opens the pause menu, and left-click picks up or places an inventory stack. If controls are rebound, use the bindings for those same actions.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for the exact release 1.20.2 and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is displayed and identifies the running version as 1.20.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, enter a recognizable disposable world name, set Game Mode to Survival, enable Allow Commands, and create the world. No particular seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins for a new Survival world with commands available.

steps.action: Wait until the world has finished loading. Do not enter the command while the loading or joining screen is still visible.
steps.success_cue: The normal in-world HUD is visible, nearby terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, capitalization, quotation marks, JSON strings, NBT braces, and final item count. Press Enter to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds without a syntax or permission error, and one gold block is added to the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the Survival inventory. Locate the newly given gold block, normally in the first available hotbar or inventory slot, and move the pointer over it without clicking.
steps.success_cue: The gold block's tooltip is visible.

steps.action: Confirm only the pre-upgrade test-item setup: the tooltip has a custom name line reading "Text" in yellow and a lore line reading "Text" in gold, with the boolean-formatted bold styling represented by the supplied command. If this input state is not present, stop and repeat the command rather than proceeding with the world update.
steps.success_cue: Before conversion, the item demonstrably contains both the supplied custom Name and supplied Lore data.

steps.action: Store the test gold block in a normal player-inventory slot. If it is in the hotbar, left-click the stack to pick it up, then left-click an empty slot in the upper 3-by-9 inventory storage grid to place it there. Do not leave it attached to the mouse pointer, in the crafting grid, or in a crafting output slot.
steps.exact_input: left-click gold block; left-click empty main-inventory slot
steps.success_cue: The gold block occupies one ordinary slot in the player's main inventory and the mouse pointer is not carrying an item.

steps.action: Press E or Esc to close the inventory without moving or discarding the test item.
steps.success_cue: The in-world HUD is visible and the test gold block is stored in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Save and Quit to Title, and wait for saving to complete.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The title screen is visible again, indicating that the 1.20.2 world session has ended and its player inventory has been saved.

steps.action: Close the 1.20.2 game client completely. Do not leave it running while starting the other version.
steps.success_cue: The 1.20.2 Java process has exited and the launcher is available.

steps.action: In the launcher, select the installation configured for the exact affected release 1.20.4 and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is displayed and identifies the running version as 1.20.4.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and single-click the same world that was created and saved in 1.20.2. Verify the selected entry has the exact test-world name; do not choose Re-Create and do not create another world.
steps.success_cue: The original 1.20.2 test-world entry is selected in the 1.20.4 world list.

steps.action: Open the selected world to initiate conversion in 1.20.4. If an upgrade confirmation is displayed, choose Create Backup and Load so the backup is created and loading proceeds; do not cancel or open a different save. If this launcher/client configuration begins loading immediately without a confirmation screen, allow that same load to continue. The backup-and-load option is the safe path when the confirmation is shown. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ADowngrading?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Play; if prompted, Create Backup and Load
steps.success_cue: The selected world's loading screen is visible and the same save is being opened by version 1.20.4.

steps.action: Wait until conversion and joining finish. Do not open the inventory or inspect the post-upgrade item yet.
steps.success_cue: The normal in-world HUD is visible in the converted save, surrounding terrain has rendered, and player movement responds normally in 1.20.4.

stor.handoff_condition: The exact world last saved in Java Edition 1.20.2 has just finished loading in Java Edition 1.20.4, including the player inventory containing the test gold block. Hand control to the observation subsystem before opening the inventory or evaluating the item's post-upgrade tooltip.
uncertainties: The report permits creation in "1.20.2 or below"; this plan uses 1.20.2 because it is the latest explicitly permitted source version and minimizes unrelated conversion changes.
The report metadata lists only 1.20.4 as an affected version, so 1.20.4 is the target even though the narrative also mentions 1.20.3 and unspecified future versions.

The report does not specify a world seed, game mode, or multiplayer requirement. A new arbitrary-seed single-player Survival world with commands enabled is selected as the minimum deterministic environment.
The report allows either player-inventory or container storage. This plan selects player-inventory storage and does not attempt the alternative container variant.

The exact presentation of the world-upgrade confirmation can vary by client flow. If no confirmation appears, initiating the load of the selected 1.20.2 save in step 13 remains the conversion trigger.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-271020:enchantment_glint_override=true does not cause pick block to avoid replacing that item
source_meta._title: Items with empty enchantments NBT tag do not upgrade as expected

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition, local singleplayer. Use the attached prebuilt world in an isolated Java Edition game directory that can be launched first with release 1.10.2 and then with snapshot 24w11a. The same saved-world folder must be preserved between launches. No dedicated server, additional players, commands, cheats, seed, coordinates, datapack, or specific game mode are stated as required.
preconditions: The Mojira attachment named "phantomenchantmentupgradetest.zip" is available to the reproduction agent.
The Minecraft Launcher can launch the exact Java Edition versions 1.10.2 and 24w11a.
Both installations are configured to use the same isolated game directory, or the agent can copy the same world folder between their respective "saves" directories.
The attached archive has been copied to a safe working location and enough disk space is available for at least two backup copies.
The test must begin with an unconverted copy of the attached world; do not begin from a copy that has already been opened in 24w11a or a newer version.
Do not substitute newly generated items for the items supplied in the attached world, because their legacy empty "Enchantments:[]" data is the subject of the conversion test.

steps.action: Obtain the attached test-world archive from the Mojira report and place it in a local working directory.
steps.success_cue: A local, readable copy of "phantomenchantmentupgradetest.zip" is present.

steps.action: Create a pristine backup copy of the downloaded ZIP before extracting or launching the world. Keep this backup outside every Minecraft "saves" directory.
steps.success_cue: An untouched backup of "phantomenchantmentupgradetest.zip" exists and can be used to restart the reproduction from the original legacy data.

steps.action: Extract the working copy of the ZIP. Open the extracted directories until reaching the actual Java world folder—the folder that directly contains "level.dat" rather than another wrapper folder.
steps.success_cue: The selected extracted world folder directly contains "level.dat" and the other world-save contents.

steps.action: Copy the extracted world folder into the isolated Java Edition game directory's "saves" folder. Typical default game-directory locations are "%APPDATA%\.minecraft" on Windows, "~/Library/Application Support/minecraft" on macOS, and "~/.minecraft" on Linux; use the configured launcher game directory instead if it was customized.
steps.success_cue: The folder containing "level.dat" is exactly one directory below the selected game directory's "saves" folder.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition 1.10.2 using the game directory containing the imported save. Do not use 1.11 through 1.20.4 for the baseline visual check, because the report states that those versions can hide the glint even though the legacy NBT remains.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running client as Minecraft 1.10.2.

steps.action: From the 1.10.2 main menu, select "Singleplayer". Locate the imported attached world by its displayed world name or by the world-folder name shown in the world list, select it, and choose "Play Selected World" or double-click it.
steps.success_cue: The attached world begins loading in Minecraft 1.10.2.

steps.action: Wait for the attached world to finish loading. Do not continue while a loading screen is displayed.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the world, nearby terrain or the prepared test area has rendered, and normal camera and movement input responds.

steps.action: Locate the legacy test items already supplied by the attached world without replacing, enchanting, crafting, moving, or otherwise modifying them. First inspect the visible hotbar at the bottom of the screen and press the inventory action—default key "E"—to inspect the player inventory. If the prepared items are instead presented in an obvious nearby container or display, use that existing presentation. Record whether they were viewed in the hotbar, player inventory, a specific container, or another display so the identical context can be reopened after upgrading.
steps.success_cue: The supplied group of "phantom enchanted" test items is visible, and its exact viewing location or container has been recorded for the second launch.

steps.action: While still in 1.10.2, visually confirm that the supplied test items display an enchantment glint. This is only the required pre-upgrade baseline. Do not alter the items after confirming it.
steps.success_cue: At least one supplied test item visibly has the animated enchantment-glint appearance in 1.10.2, and the item remains in its original slot or display location.

steps.action: Close any inventory or container interface with the inventory key or Escape, then open the pause menu with Escape and select "Save and Quit to Title" so the 1.10.2 session is saved normally.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The client has returned to the 1.10.2 title screen and the world is no longer open.

steps.action: Exit the 1.10.2 client completely. In the game directory's "saves" folder, make a backup copy of the just-closed world folder and store that copy outside "saves". Leave the original world folder in "saves" for the upgrade test.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 1.10.2 is closed, one backup of the post-baseline world exists outside "saves", and the original world remains available in "saves".

steps.action: Launch the exact affected snapshot, Minecraft: Java Edition 24w11a, using the same isolated game directory and the same world folder that was opened in 1.10.2. Do not select the fix version 24w14a.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running client as snapshot 24w11a.

steps.action: Select "Singleplayer", locate the same attached world that was previously opened in 1.10.2, and select it in the world list. Do not select a newly generated world or the backup copy stored outside "saves".
steps.success_cue: The same attached world is highlighted in the 24w11a Singleplayer world list and is ready to be opened.

steps.action: Open the selected world by choosing "Play Selected World" or double-clicking it. If 24w11a displays a version-upgrade or backup warning, proceed with opening the world only after confirming that the external backups from earlier steps exist; use the normal option that continues into the world without canceling.
steps.success_cue: 24w11a has accepted the world-open action and displays the world-loading screen.

steps.action: Wait until conversion and world loading finish. Do not interact during the loading screen, and do not continue until the prepared area has rendered and input responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside the same saved world in 24w11a, the surrounding area is rendered, and camera or movement input responds.

steps.action: Reopen the exact item-viewing context recorded in step 8 without modifying the items: press "E" if they were in the player inventory, select the same hotbar slot if they were viewed there, right-click the same nearby container if they were stored in one, or face the same existing display if that was where they were presented. Stop as soon as the supplied test items are visible and do not evaluate their appearance or data.
steps.exact_input: Use the same access input recorded in step 8; default inventory key: E; default container interaction: right-click
steps.success_cue: The same supplied legacy test items have just been presented in 24w11a and are ready for the separate observation subsystem to inspect.

stor.handoff_condition: The same attached world has been opened and fully loaded in 24w11a, and the supplied test items are visible in the same inventory, hotbar, container, or display context used for the 1.10.2 baseline. Hand control to the observation subsystem before moving, replacing, editing, or otherwise modifying any test item.
uncertainties: The report does not state the attached world's displayed name, folder structure, game mode, player position, or the exact item types, item count, slots, container, or display in which the test items are located.

The attachment itself could not be inspected during web verification, so the plan cannot provide a world name or a single predetermined UI action for locating the items. The executor must record and reuse the presentation found in the attached world.

The reproduction text says to use the "latest 1.20.5 snapshot" but does not name it in that sentence. The report's sole affected-version entry is 24w11a, so 24w11a is used as the affected snapshot and 24w14a is excluded because it is listed only as a fix version.

The precise wording and buttons of any world-upgrade warning shown by 24w11a are not supplied by the report; the plan therefore identifies the required outcome—continue opening the backed-up world—rather than asserting an exact warning label.

The Mojira report does not specify whether merely opening the world, loading the chunk or player data containing the items, or opening their inventory/container is the narrowest internal conversion event. Step 14 is treated as the report-supported trigger action, with loading and item presentation completed before handoff.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-270767:Leather horse armor no longer prevents horses from freezing in powder snow
source_meta._title: Upgrading a world with horses wearing leather horse armor makes the horse immune to freezing forever

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition, single-player integrated server. Create and save the source world in version 1.20.4, then open that same world in the affected version 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4 (launcher version ID 1.20.5-pre4). Creative mode with commands enabled and a Superflat world are used as deterministic setup choices because the report does not specify a game mode, seed, terrain, or server requirement. Default Java Edition controls are assumed unless rebound.
preconditions: Use an unmodified Minecraft: Java Edition client; do not use mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter horses, equipment, freezing, powder snow, commands, or world conversion.
The launcher must have installations for exactly 1.20.4 and 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4. Enable snapshot versions in the launcher installation list when selecting 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4.

Both installations must use the same game directory so the affected installation can open the world created in 1.20.4. If separate game directories are required, copy the complete world folder without modifying it.
Do not create the test world directly in 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4. The horse must be wearing leather horse armor while the world is saved in 1.20.4 and then converted by the affected version.
Do not open the test world in 24w05a or another intermediary version. Upgrade it directly from 1.20.4 to 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4.
Do not use the fix version 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 for reproduction.
This plan uses manual setup because the attached MC-270871.zip world download was named in the report but its contents were not supplied.
Default controls referenced below are T for chat, E for inventory, W for forward movement, Left Shift for dismounting, right-click for Use Item/Place Block, and Esc for the pause menu.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or verify two Java Edition installations: one using version 1.20.4 and one using 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4. The latter may be displayed by its launcher ID, 1.20.5-pre4. Configure both to use the same game directory.
steps.success_cue: The launcher installation list contains separate entries for 1.20.4 and 1.20.5-pre4, and both point to the same game directory.

steps.action: Launch the installation configured for exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.4. Do not start the pre-release installation yet.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and displays version 1.20.4.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, name the world MC-270871-repro, set Game Mode to Creative, ensure Allow Commands is ON, and select the Superflat world type. Leave the seed and all other settings at their defaults, then create the world.
steps.exact_input: World name: MC-270871-repro; Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands: ON; World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: World generation begins for a new Creative Superflat world named MC-270871-repro.

steps.action: Wait without issuing commands until the player appears in the world, surrounding terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on loaded, flat terrain and can move normally.

steps.action: Stand in an open area. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the exact summon command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A living adult horse appears approximately two blocks from the player, and chat reports successful entity summoning.

steps.action: Press T, enter the exact give command including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain a saddle.
steps.success_cue: One saddle is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press T, enter the exact give command including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain leather horse armor.
steps.success_cue: One leather horse armor item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so that the player's hand contains no item, approach the horse, aim the crosshair at its body, and right-click once to attempt to mount it.
steps.exact_input: Select empty hotbar slot; right-click horse
steps.success_cue: The player mounts the horse or the horse begins the normal taming attempt and throws the player off.

steps.action: If the horse throws the player off, keep the hand empty, approach it again, and right-click to remount. Repeat only until heart particles appear around the horse and the horse accepts the rider without immediately throwing the player off.
steps.success_cue: Heart particles have appeared and the player is seated on the now-tamed horse.

steps.action: While mounted on the tamed horse, press E to open the horse inventory. If E has been rebound, use the control assigned to Open/Close Inventory.
steps.success_cue: The horse inventory interface is open and shows the horse equipment slots together with the player's inventory.

steps.action: Move the saddle from the player's inventory into the horse equipment slot marked with a saddle icon. Use left-click to pick up the saddle and left-click the saddle slot to place it.
steps.exact_input: Left-click saddle; left-click horse saddle slot
steps.success_cue: The saddle slot contains the saddle and the horse model in the interface shows a saddle.

steps.action: Move the leather horse armor from the player's inventory into the horse equipment slot marked with a horse-armor outline. Use left-click to pick up the armor and left-click the armor slot to place it.
steps.exact_input: Left-click leather horse armor; left-click horse armor slot
steps.success_cue: The horse armor slot contains leather horse armor and the horse model in the interface shows the armor.

steps.action: Press E again to close the horse inventory and return to mounted gameplay.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, the player remains mounted, and leather horse armor is visibly rendered on the horse.

steps.action: Press the Sneak/Dismount control, Left Shift by default, once to dismount onto solid ground.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing beside the saddled horse, and the horse is still visibly wearing leather horse armor.

steps.action: While standing on flat solid ground near the horse, press T, enter the exact fill command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This replaces a 5-by-5 section of ground, four to eight blocks in the positive-X direction from the player's current position, with one layer of powder snow.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that 25 blocks were filled, and a 5-by-5 white powder-snow patch is visible nearby and flush with the surrounding ground.

steps.action: Approach the equipped horse, aim at its body, and right-click once to mount it.
steps.success_cue: The player is seated on the saddled horse and the horse movement interface is active.

steps.action: Use W and mouse movement to position the horse on ordinary solid ground directly beside the powder-snow patch. Do not enter the powder snow yet.
steps.success_cue: The mounted horse is adjacent to the powder-snow patch but all four of its legs remain over normal solid ground.

steps.action: Press Left Shift once to dismount beside the horse. Confirm visually one final time that the horse is still wearing leather horse armor before saving the 1.20.4 world.
steps.success_cue: The player, the leather-armored horse, and the powder-snow patch are all present in the same loaded area, with the horse standing outside the powder snow.

steps.action: Press Esc and select Save and Quit to Title. Wait until the Singleplayer world list or title screen has fully returned; do not force-close the game while the world is saving.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The world is closed normally and MC-270871-repro is visible in the saved-world list.

steps.action: Create a safety backup while still running 1.20.4: select MC-270871-repro in the Singleplayer list, choose Edit, then choose Make Backup. Wait for the backup-complete notification before continuing.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft reports that a backup of MC-270871-repro was created.

steps.action: Return to the title screen, choose Quit Game, and wait until the 1.20.4 process has fully closed. In the launcher, select and launch the installation for exactly 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4, identified by launcher version ID 1.20.5-pre4.
steps.success_cue: The new Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running build as 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4 or 1.20.5-pre4.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and open the existing world MC-270871-repro. Do not create a replacement world. If Minecraft displays a warning about opening or upgrading the world in a development version, choose the option that creates a backup and loads the world, or otherwise explicitly confirms loading the existing world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> MC-270871-repro -> Create Backup and Load/confirm load if prompted
steps.success_cue: The existing 1.20.4 world begins loading under 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4.

steps.action: Wait until world conversion and loading finish. Do not interact with the horse until surrounding chunks are rendered and player movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player has loaded near the saved location, the terrain and powder-snow patch are rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Locate the same horse beside the powder-snow patch. Confirm that it still has its saddle and that leather horse armor is visibly equipped after conversion. Do not replace, remove, or modify its equipment with commands.
steps.success_cue: The converted horse from the 1.20.4 world is visible near the test patch, with both its saddle and leather horse armor still equipped.

steps.action: Approach the converted horse, aim at its body, and right-click once to mount it.
steps.success_cue: The player is seated on the converted horse and can control it using the saddle.

steps.action: While mounted, press E to open the horse inventory.
steps.success_cue: The converted horse's inventory is open, with the saddle and leather horse armor visible in their equipment slots.

steps.action: Unequip only the leather horse armor. Left-click the leather horse armor in the horse armor slot, then left-click an empty slot in the player's inventory to store it. Leave the saddle equipped and do not put any other item into the horse armor slot.
steps.exact_input: Left-click equipped leather horse armor; left-click empty player inventory slot
steps.success_cue: The horse armor slot is visibly empty, the leather horse armor is in the player's inventory, and the saddle remains in the horse's saddle slot.

steps.action: Press E to close the horse inventory. Do not dismount.
steps.success_cue: Mounted gameplay resumes, the player remains seated on the horse, and no horse armor is visibly rendered on it.

steps.action: Use W and mouse movement to ride the horse from the solid ground into the center of the 5-by-5 powder-snow patch. Continue only until the horse is clearly occupying powder snow rather than standing at its edge.
steps.success_cue: The mounted horse is inside the powder-snow patch, away from the edge, with its horse armor slot still empty.

steps.action: Release W and all other movement inputs so the mounted horse remains in the powder snow. Do not steer it back onto ordinary ground.
steps.success_cue: The player remains mounted and the horse is stationary within the powder-snow patch.

steps.action: While still mounted on the horse in powder snow, press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not run it from a server console because the executing player must have the horse as its vehicle.
steps.exact_input: /execute on vehicle run data get entity @s
steps.success_cue: Chat returns entity-data output for the mounted horse rather than reporting that no vehicle or entity was found; the horse remains mounted and inside the powder snow.

stor.handoff_condition: The world has been converted directly from 1.20.4 to 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4; the original horse's visible leather horse armor has been removed while its saddle remains equipped; the player is mounted on that horse; the horse is stationary inside the powder-snow patch; and `/execute on vehicle run data get entity @s` has just returned the mounted horse's entity data. Begin observation without moving the horse out of the powder snow or changing its equipment.
uncertainties: The report says to upgrade to the 'latest version.' This plan resolves that historical wording to 1.20.5 Pre-Release 4 because it is the only listed affected version. The listed fix version, 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1, is intentionally not used.

The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, terrain type, or whether cheats are enabled. Creative mode, commands, and a Superflat world are practical setup choices used to obtain a deterministic horse and powder-snow test area without exploration.
The attachment MC-270871.zip is not available in the supplied report contents, so the optional downloaded-world path is not used.

The report does not specify how long the horse should remain in powder snow before evaluation. The plan hands control to the observation subsystem immediately after the diagnostic command while the horse remains stationary in powder snow.

The `/summon`, `/give`, and `/fill` commands are setup conveniences not supplied by the report. They are executed only in 1.20.4 and do not replace the required manual taming, equipment, world-conversion, unequipping, or powder-snow entry sequence.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 25w18a in a single-player integrated-server world. Use a newly created Creative-mode test world for deterministic item access. No particular seed, coordinates, sign wood type, graphics setting, GPU, dedicated server, or multiplayer client is required by the report. The instructions assume the default keyboard-and-mouse controls and an English-language item search.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher must be able to start the exact affected snapshot, 25w18a. Enable historical snapshot versions in the launcher's installation/profile settings if 25w18a is not initially available.
Use a disposable test world. The minimal procedure tests a newly placed sign, so no existing or upgraded world is required.
Keep the game window focused so keyboard input is sent to Minecraft.
Do not use the fixed version 25w19a for this reproduction.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher and navigate to the installation/profile management screen. Enable snapshot versions if the version selector does not currently show historical snapshots.
steps.success_cue: The launcher permits snapshot versions to be selected when creating or editing an installation.

steps.action: Create or edit an installation and select the exact game version named "snapshot 25w18a". Save the installation without substituting another snapshot or release.
steps.success_cue: The saved launcher installation identifies 25w18a as its selected version.

steps.action: Start the 25w18a installation and wait for Minecraft to reach the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is responsive and displays 25w18a as the running version.

steps.action: From the title screen, select "Singleplayer", then select "Create New World" to open the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is open.

steps.action: Optionally name the test world "MC-297339 reproduction", set Game Mode to Creative, leave the seed unspecified, and select "Create New World".
steps.success_cue: World generation begins for a new Creative-mode world.

steps.action: Wait until world generation and initial chunk loading finish. Do not continue while a loading screen is present or terrain is still failing to render.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press the inventory action key, which is E by default, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and includes item-selection tabs and the player hotbar.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, focus its search field, and enter "oak sign". If the inventory is already on the searchable item tab, use its visible search field directly.
steps.success_cue: The filtered item results include the regular item named Oak Sign.

steps.action: Move one Oak Sign stack from the search results into any empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine quick-access slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: An Oak Sign is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Escape, then select the hotbar slot containing the Oak Sign by pressing its corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E, then the Oak Sign hotbar slot number
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and the Oak Sign is shown as the currently held item.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the top face of a nearby solid block, such as a grass or stone block with empty space above it. Press the Use Item/Place Block control, which is the right mouse button by default, once to place a regular standing oak sign.
steps.success_cue: A standing oak sign has been placed and the sign-editing interface is open with its confirmation button available. Keep this interface open.

steps.action: Without closing the sign-editing interface or changing focus to another window, type the test string "TEST123" once. Do not select the confirmation button yet and do not press Escape.
steps.success_cue: The TEST123 keystrokes have been sent while the newly placed sign's editing interface remains open; no additional player or UI action has been taken.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just entered the test keystrokes TEST123 into the active editing interface of a newly placed regular oak sign in 25w18a. The sign-editing interface remains open and no confirmation or cancellation action has been performed; begin observation in this state.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a formal numbered Steps to Reproduce section. This plan reconstructs the minimum new-sign procedure directly supported by the description.
The report does not specify a required game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a deterministic way to obtain a sign without crafting or commands.

The report states that all regular and hanging sign types are affected but does not require a particular wood type. A regular Oak Sign placed on the top of a solid block is used as the simplest deterministic representative.
The report does not specify the text to enter. TEST123 is a practical test string chosen to provide unmistakable keyboard input.

The description also reports a separate world-upgrade variant involving pre-existing signs placed before updating to 25w18a. That variant is not included because the same report explicitly states that newly placed signs reproduce the issue, allowing a shorter deterministic procedure.

The report mentions both single-player and a third-party hosted server. This plan uses single-player because the report confirms that a dedicated or third-party server is not necessary for the new-sign reproduction.
